meta.title: Southwest Flies Only One Type Of Plane. It's Saving Them Hundreds Of Millions.
meta.hook: Southwest Airlines operates hundreds of aircraft, and every single one is the same plane.
meta.description: Southwest Airlines has built its entire fleet around one aircraft family, the Boeing 737. That single decision means one training program for pilots and mechanics, one set of spare parts to stock, and total flexibility to swap crews and aircraft across routes. Airlines with mixed fleets carry all of that complexity multiplied by however many aircraft types they fly.

scenes.narration: Southwest Airlines operates hundreds of aircraft, and every single one is the same plane.

visual.visual_intent: A commercial jet lined up on a runway at golden hour, low angle, cinematic
visual.decision_reason: hook beat: the plane itself, hard cut

scenes.narration: One aircraft type, the Boeing seven thirty-seven, across the entire fleet, on every route they fly.

visual.visual_intent: Multiple identical passenger jets parked at gates, wide airport tarmac shot, daylight

scenes.narration: Most airlines fly several aircraft types, which means separate training, separate parts inventories, separate maintenance crews for each one.

visual.visual_intent: Mechanics working under an aircraft in a large maintenance hangar, industrial light, wide shot

scenes.narration: Southwest collapses all of that into one system. Any pilot can fly any plane in the fleet.

visual.visual_intent: Two pilots in a cockpit going through preflight checks, focused, natural cabin light

scenes.narration: That flexibility means fewer delays from aircraft mismatches, and simpler scheduling across the whole airline.

visual.visual_intent: An airport departures board with on-time flight statuses, sharp digital light

scenes.narration: Southwest estimates the strategy saves it hundreds of millions of dollars a year, all from refusing to diversify its fleet. Follow for more.

visual.visual_intent: A wide aerial view of an airline's tarmac full of identical jets, dusk light, cinematic
